'''Christian Gavina''' (born January 27, 1979) is a Filipino professional [[basketball]] coach.

== Early life and college career ==
Gavina was born in the Philippines and migrated to Jersey City, New Jersey when he was three years old.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsportsasia.com/basketball/291492/qa-manny-pacquiaos-new-deputy-coach-chris-gavina/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107031734/http://www.foxsportsasia.com/basketball/291492/qa-manny-pacquiaos-new-deputy-coach-chris-gavina/|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 7, 2017|title=Q&A with Manny Pacquiao's new deputy coach Chris Gavina|work=Fox Sports Philippines}}</ref> He played college basketball for the [[Stevens Institute of Technology]] in Hoboken, New Jersey. He finished second in all-time scoring for the school and have his jersey number retired after his graduation in 2001.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lintag|first=Paul|url=http://sports.abs-cbn.com/basketball/news/2017/04/13/from-lab-chris-gavina-s-unconventional-way-pba-24583|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170415181443/http://sports.abs-cbn.com/basketball/news/2017/04/13/from-lab-chris-gavina-s-unconventional-way-pba-24583|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 15, 2017|title=From the Lab: Chris Gavina's unconventional way to the PBA|work=ABS-CBN Sports|date=April 13, 2017}}</ref>

After graduation, he worked as a formulation chemist for [[L'Oreal]] from 2004 to 2008 and then moved back to the Philippines to pursue a career in basketball. He first played for the Quezon Red Oilers and the Mandaue-Cebu Landmasters of the defunct [[Liga Pilipinas]].

==Coaching career==
After his contract expired with Mandaue, he returned to the United States and earned a strength and conditioning coach certification at the Institute of Sports and Science. He returned to Manila and got a job for [[ASEAN Basketball League|ABL's]] [[AirAsia Philippine Patriots]]' as their strength and conditioning coach in 2011. When the Patriots were disbanded in 2012, he then moved to [[GlobalPort Batang Pier]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association|PBA]].

In 2016, Gavina was named as the first assistant coach of [[Manny Pacquiao]] for the [[Mahindra Floodbuster]], replacing [[Chito Victolero]]. Although Pacquiao is named as the head coach of the Floodbuster, Gavina ran the day-to-day practices and acted as the head coach in Pacquiao's absence.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/news/mahindra-names-chgavina-to-replace-victolero-as-trade-deals-remain-on-hold|title=Chris Gavina named Mahindra coach to replace Victolero as trades remain on hold|work=Spin.ph|date=April 29, 2016}}</ref>

After Pacquiao's contract as player-coach in Mahindra (later renamed as Kia Picanto in 2017) expired after the 2016–17 season, Gavina was named as the head coach of the Picanto.<ref>{{cite news|last=Leongson|first=Randolph|url=http://sports.inquirer.net/271088/kia-signs-little-known-hungry-players-part-unconventional-mentality|title=Kia signs up little known but 'hungry' players as part of 'unconventional mentality|newspaper=Philippine Daily Inquirer|date=November 4, 2017}}</ref>

On 2018, Gavina returned to PBA after being tapped as an assistant coach of the Rain or Shine Elasto Painters.<ref>{{cite web|last=Marquez|first=CJ|url=https://cnnphilippines.com/sports/2018/11/16/Chris-Gavina-Rain-or-Shine-assistant-coach-PBA.html|title=Chris Gavina makes PBA comeback as part of Rain or Shine coaching staff|work=CNN Philippines|date=November 16, 2018|accessdate=August 23, 2020|archive-date=July 1, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230701080712/https://www.cnnphilippines.com/sports/2018/11/16/Chris-Gavina-Rain-or-Shine-assistant-coach-PBA.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On October 25, 2022, Gavina signed with the [[Taichung Suns]] of the [[T1 League]] for head coach.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sports.ltn.com.tw/news/breakingnews/4101017|title=台中太陽找菲律賓教練執教 洋將補進得分王仕東|date=October 25, 2022|work=Liberty Times Net|access-date=October 25, 2022}}</ref> On June 29, 2023, Gavina left the [[Taichung Suns]].<ref>{{cite news |title=台中太陽將再尋主帥！菲籍總教練克里斯離隊 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2530030 |accessdate=June 29, 2023 |work=ETtoday |date=June 29, 2023}}</ref>

Gavina was named as the head coach of the [[UE Red Warriors basketball|UE Red Warriors]] on February 13, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=INQUIRER.net |date=2025-02-13 |title=UAAP: Chris Gavina appointed new UE Red Warriors coach |url=https://sports.inquirer.net/607419/uaap-chris-gavina-appointed-new-ue-red-warriors-coach |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=INQUIRER.net |language=en}}</ref> On his [[UAAP Season 88 basketball tournaments|first UAAP season]], Gavina, after a loss against the [[De La Salle Green Archers basketball|De La Salle Green Archers]], launched an expletive-riddled rant at the post-game press conference.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chris Gavina blasts UAAP referees with expletive-filled rant |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/uaap-men/chris-gavina-blasts-uaap-referees-with-expletive-filled-rant-a5172-20251015 |access-date=2025-12-02 |website=Spin.ph |language=en}}</ref> The UAAP then suspended Gavina for four games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fuertes |first=Rommel Jr |date=2025-10-18 |title=UAAP suspends UE coach Chris Gavina for four games |url=https://sports.inquirer.net/644811/uaap-suspends-ue-coach-chris-gavina-for-four-games |access-date=2025-10-19 |website=INQUIRER.net |language=en}}</ref> UE finished the season winless after 14 games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Terrado |first=Jonas |date=2025-11-22 |title=UAAP: FEU keeps Final Four bid alive, sends UE to 0-14 season |url=https://sports.inquirer.net/649406/uaap-feu-keeps-final-four-bid-alive-sends-ue-to-0-14-season |access-date=2025-12-02 |website=INQUIRER.net |language=en}}</ref> In [[UAAP Season 89 basketball tournaments|2026]], UE started the season on a 0–2 record. Gavina then resigned prior to their third game, being replaced by [[Paulo Hubalde]]. The Warriors were in the midst of a 22-game losing streak when he resigned.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gavina steps down as UE coach; Hubalde steps up on interim basis |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/uaap-men/chris-gavina-out-paulo-hubalde-in-as-ue-head-coach-a2437-20260926 |access-date=2026-09-27 |website=Spin.ph |language=en}}</ref>
